blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At senior level, cost accounting is a strategic frame — the way the executive team decides which products deserve investment, which prices are defensible, and which customers are quietly subsidised by others. The questions at this level are uncomfortable. Are our profitable products actually profitable, or do they merely rely on allocation rules that flatter them? Are our unprofitable ones truly losing money, or carrying costs that would not disappear if we closed them tomorrow?

Good senior cost work is honest before it is optimised. Allocations are defensible. Assumptions are written down. Comparisons are kept stable across years, so that a decision made today can be judged fairly next year. The numbers are not arranged to justify a conclusion already reached — they are built to survive scrutiny.

Cost accounting, used this way, produces decisions the executive team can defend, internally and externally, and that survive uncomfortable follow-up questions six months later. It is a discipline more than a calculation, and the senior leaders who understand the difference tend to make far fewer expensive mistakes.

items.q: According to the text, what is cost accounting at senior level?
options: A calculation owned by the finance department alone
A strategic frame for investment, pricing and product decisions
items.why: "cost accounting is a strategic frame — the way the executive team decides which products deserve investment, which prices are defensible…"

items.q: What does the text suggest about a product that looks profitable?
options: It should immediately have its price raised
It has no bearing on strategy
Its profitability may rest on allocation rules that flatter it
It is always the safest product to invest in
items.why: "do they merely rely on allocation rules that flatter them?" — o lucro pode ser um artefato da alocação.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Comparisons should stay stable from one year to the next.
Assumptions behind cost figures should be written down.
A good cost decision must survive later scrutiny.
Numbers should be arranged to justify the conclusion leadership prefers.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que os números não são arrumados para justificar uma conclusão já tomada — são feitos para resistir ao escrutínio.

items.q: Why does the text ask whether an unprofitable product's costs "would not disappear if we closed them tomorrow"?
options: To argue that unprofitable products should never be closed
To prove that closing products always saves money
To suggest some losses come from costs that would simply be reallocated, not removed
To show that allocation rules are irrelevant
items.why: Inferência: se o custo permanece mesmo fechando o produto, o 'prejuízo' pode ser um custo carregado, não um custo evitável.

items.q: What does "It is a discipline more than a calculation" most strongly imply?
options: Discipline and calculation mean the same thing here
The value lies in rigour and judgement, not in the arithmetic itself
Calculations are unnecessary at senior level
Only trained accountants may interpret the numbers
items.why: Inferência: 'disciplina' aponta para honestidade, consistência e defensibilidade — não para a mera conta.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver apresentando a revisão de custos à liderança. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Before I show you the revised figures, let me set expectations. Two products that this board has treated as reliably profitable are, on honest allocations, losing money. I want to walk you through why — and I want the assumptions on the screen, not buried in a footnote.

The old model pushed a large share of shared overhead onto a single high-volume line, which flattered everything else. Once I distributed those costs on a defensible basis — actual usage, not convenience — the picture inverted. The point is not that the products are bad. It is that the numbers we were defending would not have survived a serious follow-up question.

So here is what I would ask of you. Do not reach for a decision this afternoon. Sit with the reclassification, test my assumptions, and if they hold, we build the pricing conversation on top of them. If they do not, tell me where the logic breaks and I will rework it.

Whatever we conclude, I would like us to keep the method stable, so that next year we are comparing like with like, and a decision we take today can be judged fairly six months from now.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is the headline finding Oliver presents?
options: The company must raise every price immediately
Two products treated as profitable are actually losing money on honest allocations
The finance model is beyond repair
items.why: "Two products that this board has treated as reliably profitable are, on honest allocations, losing money."

items.q: Why did the old model make other products look better than they were?
options: It pushed a large share of shared overhead onto one high-volume line
items.why: "The old model pushed a large share of shared overhead onto a single high-volume line, which flattered everything else."

items.q: What does Oliver ask the board to do this afternoon?
options: Not reach a decision, but test his assumptions first
Approve the new pricing on the spot
items.why: "Do not reach for a decision this afternoon. Sit with the reclassification, test my assumptions…"

items.q: When Oliver says the numbers "would not have survived a serious follow-up question," he implies…
options: the old figures would have collapsed under honest scrutiny
the products should be discontinued at once
the old figures were defensible but unpopular
items.why: Inferência: 'não sobreviveriam' = a defesa dos números ruiria diante de perguntas sérias — eram frágeis, não honestos.

items.q: How would you best describe Oliver's stance toward the board?
options: Rigorous but open — he invites challenge to his own assumptions
Indifferent to whether the board agrees
Certain that no further work is needed
Defensive and unwilling to be questioned
items.why: Inferência: ele expõe as premissas na tela e pede que testem — postura rigorosa, mas aberta ao contraditório.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Treated as a strategic frame, cost accounting shapes where we invest." A strategic frame is…
options: a way of framing decisions to guide strategy
items.why: Strategic frame = enquadramento estratégico: a lente pela qual a estratégia é decidida.

items.q: "A price is defensible when…" it is…
options: set by the sales team alone
one you can justify and stand behind under scrutiny
the highest the market will bear
items.why: Defensible = defensável: sustenta-se diante de perguntas e escrutínio.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Under the old rules, one product was quietly ___ by the profits of another."
items.why: To subsidise = subsidiar: um produto banca os custos de outro.

items.q: "Those overheads were assigned by a convenient allocation rule." An allocation rule is…
options: a rule about who signs contracts
a method for distributing shared costs across products
items.why: Allocation rule = regra de alocação: como os custos compartilhados são distribuídos.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Loading overhead onto one line ___ the margins of everything else, making them look healthier than they were."
items.why: To flatter = favorecer/embelezar: fazer os números parecerem melhores do que são.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões de custos e pricing. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the reclassification before we act." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on Oliver's new allocation." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Honest numbers should hold up when the board questions them next quarter." To hold up means to…
items.why: Hold up = sustentar-se, resistir ao escrutínio.

items.q: "Once the allocations are agreed, we build on them to set price." To build on means to…
options: use them as a foundation for the next step
items.why: Build on = usar como base para o passo seguinte.

items.q: "A cosmetic tweak to the model won't move the needle on real profitability." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
